findings.title: Method <-> MethodSet static-initializer cycle can deadlock two threads on first use
findings.description: Method.<clinit> builds ANY = MethodSet.of(...) (Method.java:12) so initializing Method needs MethodSet initialized, while MethodSet.<clinit> evaluates METHODS = Method.values() (MethodSet.java:15) so initializing MethodSet needs Method initialized. If thread A first touches Method (e.g. Method.GET / Method.valueOf in an adapter or app thread) while thread B first touches MethodSet (e.g. app.route(Method.get().post(), ...) or MethodSet.of), each holds one class-init lock and waits for the other: permanent JVM-level hang with no exception. Reproduced by compiling just Method.java + MethodSet.java and releasing two threads from a CyclicBarrier (Class.forName of each): 1 of 6 JVM runs hung (DEADLOCK after 3 s join). Single-threaded first use is fine, which is why per-wave tests never saw it.
findings.suggested_fix: Break the cycle in one direction: drop the static METHODS array from MethodSet and use Method.values() inside the iterator (or a lazy holder class), so MethodSet.<clinit> never touches Method; or move ANY into a lazy holder inside Method. Add a regression test that initializes both classes from two threads in a fresh class loader.

findings.title: ServerHandle.address() javadoc says the bound address is always 127.0.0.1, code and docs/api return the configured bindAddress
findings.description: Javadoc: 'The bound address, 127.0.0.1.' DefaultRestApp.java:521 returns settings.bindAddress(), and docs/api/app.md:203 says it is the configured value (default 127.0.0.1). With app.server(o -> o.bindAddress("0.0.0.0")) address() returns "0.0.0.0", so an IDE user reading the javadoc builds a client URL assuming loopback.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the javadoc to 'The address the server was bound with: the configured bind address, 127.0.0.1 by default.'

findings.title: Response.header javadoc says 'Adds a header' but the implementation replaces a same-name header
findings.description: Javadoc on Response.header: 'Adds a header; returns this response.' DefaultResponse.header (internal/DefaultResponse.java:375-386) documents and implements Express res.set semantics: put(name, value) replaces any same-name header (case-insensitive), and docs/api/response.md says the same. A caller who reads only the javadoc and calls res.header("Link", a).header("Link", b) expecting two header lines silently loses the first (only addCookie appends).
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to 'Sets a header, replacing a same-name header (as Express res.set); only addCookie appends a repeatable header.'

findings.title: UploadFile.bytes() and MultipartOptions.tempDirectory javadoc omit documented limits and exceptions
findings.description: UploadFile.bytes() javadoc says 'The whole content in memory.' while docs/api/multipart.md says it throws IllegalStateException for a part over 8 MiB (8388608 bytes); likewise save()/inputStream() on a part whose request already ended throw IllegalStateException (docs only), and MultipartOptions.tempDirectory(File) (MultipartOptions.java:26-27) does not say a null dir throws NullPointerException (MultipartSettings.java:85, docs multipart.md). A Java/Kotlin caller relying on the javadoc calls bytes() on a large upload and gets an unexpected ISE.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the 8 MiB / IllegalStateException contract to UploadFile.bytes(), the 'unusable after the request ends' note to inputStream/save/transferTo/bytes, and 'null throws NullPointerException' to tempDirectory.

findings.title: ServerOptions javadoc 'no value means unlimited' contradicts docs/api (there is no unlimited value)
findings.description: ServerOptions class javadoc ends 'and no value means unlimited'. docs/api/app.md:131 states no value means unlimited (each setter rejects 0/negative/over-max with IllegalArgumentException; DefaultServerOptions.range enforces 1..max). Read literally the sentence suggests that leaving a limit unset is unlimited, whereas an unset limit takes the stated default. MultipartOptions/SseOptions/WebSocketOptions phrase this correctly ('There is no unlimited value').
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with 'there is no unlimited value; an unset setting keeps the default shown on its setter.'

findings.title: docs/api/lifecycle.md ServiceRegistry/ApplicationContext listing drops @Nullable that the code (and Kotlin T?) has
findings.description: The documented interfaces show '<T> T getOrNull(Class<T> type);' and '<T> T attribute(String key, Class<T> type);' and 'void attribute(String key, Object value);' without @Nullable, but ServiceRegistry.getOrNull (ServiceRegistry.java:19), ApplicationContext.attribute(key, Class) (ApplicationContext.java:16) return @Nullable T and attribute(key, value) takes @Nullable Object. Kotlin users see T? (kotlin.md table says req.attribute is T?); the lifecycle page reads as non-null T and contradicts it. CLAUDE.md requires docs/api to follow API changes.
findings.suggested_fix: Add import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable and the @Nullable markers to the listing, as multipart.md already does for UploadFile.
